title: Bent hockey-stick stock–recruitment function
content:
Abstract
The hockey-stick model is a simple and widely applicable stock–recruitment function. One drawback is its non-differentiability at the breakpoint, which can be especially problematic when using state-space models for stock assessment. Here, we develop a new bent hockey-stick model that retains a differentiable breakpoint. We also propose a new algorithm for estimating maximum sustainable yield under multiplicative process stochasticity in the stock–recruitment relationship, where stochastic variation, typically represented by a log-normal error term, acts multiplicatively on the deterministic process. Simulation studies demonstrate the utility of these approaches, which can substantially enhance the robustness and sustainability of fisheries management.
